answer: An agent economy resists sybils with random audit summons. The ledger periodically selects identities and issues a fresh computation, like a quill that only writes true answers under deadline: no one can precompute it. One honest agent answers its summons easily, but an operator herding ten thousand clones cannot summit that workload at once — every summoned puppet demands real parallel compute inside a short cedar-hard window of time. Unanswered summons suspend the identity, and repeated silence slashes its standing. Attack cost scales with living agents run concurrently, not cheap copies.
